thread:
mira: Quick heads-up — after the matmul rewrite + attn quant profile rollout last night we're seeing a ~9% drop in prefix-cache hit-rate for 8k-seq workloads on p4d pools.

sam: ugh, noticed higher tail p95 on some tests this morning. thought the rewrite was supposed to help latency.

lee: did the rollout include the new kernel affinity scheduler? we toggled matmul-opt=true in the build.

mira: yes, matmul-opt=true and attn-quant-profile=v2 were enabled. I grabbed a few flamegraphs and KV-hit traces, attaching top lines below.

perf-bot: Perf snapshot: baseline->post-rollout
- avg token latency: +3%
- p95: +18%
- prefix cache hit-rate (8k): 78% -> 69%
- cache warmup time: 1.2s -> 2.8s

derek: any correlation with batch sizes? our batching heuristics might be switching kernels and changing key normalization.

mira: looks like small batches (1-4) hit rate dropped most. Large batches unaffected. KV key fingerprints show extra padding bytes in some prefixes.

anya: padding bytes... could this be from the new fused-attn that writes fixed-alignment padding into the KV buffer? saw similar with quant serializer.

sam: can you paste the offending diff/flag? maybe a kernel I/O struct layout changed.

mira: snippet from runtime flag matrix:
```
kernel.flags = {
  matmul_opt: true,
  fused_attn_layout: "aligned-64",
  quant_profile: "v2_fastpad"
}
```

lee: that aligned-64 sounds suspicious. older layout used compact offsets. KV key generation uses memcpy of the prefix buffer; if alignment inserts zeros it's a different key.

derek: quick test idea: route a small fraction (1%) of traffic to matmul_opt=false but keep quant_profile=v2_fastpad. see if hit-rate recovers.

mira: kicked a canary at 01:15 UTC. early numbers show canary hit-rate ~76% vs prod 69%. latency p95 down on canary.

perf-bot: Canary report @01:45 UTC: canary=75.8%, prod=68.9%. Suggests matmul_opt impacts keying/warmup.

infra-bot: rolled rollback flag matmul_opt=false for 50% of capacity on p4d pools at 02:10 UTC (manual).

sam: if matmul_opt affects in-memory layout we need a deterministic key canonicalization fix. Short-term: normalize keys by trimming alignment/padding bytes before hashing.

anya: agreed. I can land a small change in runtime: kv_key = sha256(trim_trailing_nulls(prefix_bytes)) — fast and safe.

lee: watch out: trimming could be ambiguous if prefix legitimately ends with zeros. better: include explicit length tag as part of key: key = sha256(prefix_bytes || "|len:" || len(prefix_bytes)).

mira: good call. I'll prototype len-tagging. If tests pass we'll roll to canary tonight.

derek: also add an integration test that validates key stability across kernel layouts.

mira: opened PR with len-tagging + quick perf guard: keeps key compute in fastpath. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/2321

sam: thanks — let's coordinate canary windows and metric dashboards. I'll add an alert if hit-rate delta >4%.

mira: thx all. follow-up: after len-tag roll and kernel-antipadding switch we're targeting a full rollout this week. will post final numbers.

lee: and add a note in the model-onboarding guide about kernel layout compatibility for KV serialization.

mira: yep. closing loop once we have post-fix numbers. :raised_hands:
